rows: Port. What shall I say you are? / L. Bard. Tell thou the earl
And he himself will answer. / L. Bard. Here comes the earl.
And bears down all before him. / L. Bard. Noble earl,
North. Good, an God will! / L. Bard. As good as heart can wish:
Since Cæsar's fortunes ! / North. How is this derived?
Staying no longer question. / North. Ha! Again:
Had met ill luck? / L. Bard. My lord, I’Il tell you what;
Give then such instances of loss? / L. Bard. Who, he ?
To fright our party. / North. How doth my son and brother?
But, for my lord your son,— / North. Why, he is dead.
Hast. With him, we may. / L. Bard. Yea, marry, there’s the point:
Need not be dreaded. / Hast. If he should do so,
I have no certain notice. / Arch. Let us on,
Have talk’d of Monmouth’s grave. / North. Beshrew your heart,
And find me worse provided. / Lady N. O, fly to Scotland, 5e
Unless on you. / King. Are these things then necessities?
Are fifty thousand strong. / War. It cannot be, my lord;
Unto your sickness. / King. I will take your counsel:
Hast. We have sent forth already. / Arch. "Tis well done.
And dash themselves to pieces. / Hast. Now, what news?
What doth concern your coming? / West. Then, my lord,
Upon our honours ? / West. O, my good Lord Mowbray,
Which must decide it. / Arch. My lord, we will do so. [Exit West
May offer, but not hold. / Arch. Tis very true:
Grow stronger for the breaking. / Mozob. Be it so.
Have here up-swarm’d them. / Arch. Good my Lord of Lancaster,
To the last man. / Hast. And though we here fall down,
Arch. I do not doubt you. / West. I am glad of it.
And neither party loser. / Lan. Go, my lord,
We should have coped withal. / Arch. Go, good Lord Hastings,
Arch. Will you thus break your faith? / Lan. I pawn’d thee none:
Shall soon enjoy. / King. Humphrey, my son of Moucester,
King. And how accompanied? / Glou. I do not know, my lord.
Glou. Comfort, your majesty! / Clar. O my royal father!
War. Less noise, less noise! / Prince. Who saw the Duke of Clarence?
Glou. Exceeding ill. / Prince. Heard he the good news yet?
Where is my Lord of Warwick? / Prince. My Lord of Warwick!
Ch. Just. I hope, not dead. / War. He’s walk’d the way of nature;
Shal. Under King Harry. / Pist. Harry the Fourth? or Fifth?
Shal. Harry the Fourth. / Pist. A foutre for thine office!
